newsitem.title: MEXICO: Clinton to meet with Mexico's opposition leaders.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to meet with Mexico's opposition leaders.

text.p: Mexico's top two oppostition parties were expected to hold unprecedented meetings with U.S. President Bill Clinton late on Tuesday and planned to discuss immigration and the war on drugs, a party leader said.

"It is the first time in history...that a president of the United States has a dialogue with the opposition," Andres Lopez Obrador, president of the left-leaning Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), told the Radio Red radio network.
The PRD and the conservative National Action Party (PAN) said they would raise the thorny topic of immigration when they see Clinton, who is on his first state visit to Mexico.
PAN President Felipe Calderon also told Radio Red he intended to discuss drug abuse in the United States and U.S.-Mexican oil drilling limits in the Gulf of Mexico.

"There is not only an anti-immigrant sentiment in the United States, but also an anti-Mexican one," Calderon said. He said only 40 percent of immigrants in the United States were Mexican but 90 percent of deportations were Mexican nationals.
Both the PAN and the PRD have made recent inroads into breaking the 66-year grip on power held by President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Among election gains, the PAN has a handful of state governorships and the PRD was expected to win the first-ever race for the important post of Mexico City mayor in July.
Calderon will be accompanied by the PAN governors for the border states of Chihuahua and Baja California, Francisco Barrio Terrazas and Hector Teran.
The PRD's secretary-general Jesus Ortega and the party's international affairs spokesman Ricardo Pascoe will join Lopez Obrador.
